steps.what: See the tray or hear the items before the cash registers are used.
Key the items onto the cash registers.
Take payment on the cash registers and count any change.

tasks.design: The attendant still sees the tray and still takes payment on the {OTHER} cash register, including cash, the card terminal and a line that does not match the tray. The keying step is the only one that shortens: lines the server already entered for that table are not keyed again, and preset keys cover coffee, water and condiments. A cafeteria tray with no prior check is still keyed while the attendant looks at it. The register is not used to time or score the attendant, and the screen shows item name, quantity and price only.
tasks.previous_blocker: The items lived on a paper docket or in the server's head, so the attendant keyed the whole sale while the guest waited.
tasks.enabler_now: The same register can list a check the server already entered, and can carry preset keys for the few items this station sells all day. No new system is required.
tasks.still_hard: A cafeteria tray is not on a check until this attendant keys it. Taking payment, counting change and a disputed price stay at the drawer.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant can see that the tray and the lines do not match, and can stop before the guest pays the wrong amount.
tasks.altitude: The attendant still runs the register in front of the guest. The only change is that some lines are already on the check.

reach.task: Enter the table's items before the attendant reaches the register
reach.learn: Which lines are already stored, so only the missing ones are keyed.

reach.task: Keep the preset keys equal to the current menu
reach.learn: Which button sells which item, and to refuse a key that charges the wrong one.

evidence.claim: A register can list an open check by table and can carry preset keys for common items. Model knowledge. That does not take the payment.
Works-council consent applies only if the system is also used to watch staff attendance or performance, and only where a works council exists.
An allergy note is health data. Outside healthcare, processing it usually needs explicit consent, so the payment screen does not show it.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task starts when the attendant is at the cash register with a tray or a table to settle, and ends when payment is taken. It does not take the food order and it does not cook.

Open-check contract, read only on the keying step: table id, item id, quantity, price. Producer: the server, at order entry, on the same register. If no check exists, the attendant keys from the tray inside that step. No step at zero remaining time reads the check.
Preset-key contract: button and item id. Producer: the restaurant supervisor when the menu changes. Fallback: the attendant searches the register list inside the same keying step.
The register view shows item name, quantity and price. Allergy text stays on the kitchen ticket. The design adds no report of the attendant's speed.

Remaining time on the keying step assumes presets exist and that some dining-room checks are already entered. The saved range is a cafeteria tray with no prior lines. Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 is a check of the preset keys after a menu change.
unknowns: Whether servers in this house enter items before the attendant reaches the register, or the attendant keys every cafeteria tray.
Whether a void or a discount needs a supervisor here. A typical sale in this task does not.
Whether a works council exists and has already consented to the register. This design adds no staff-performance view.
research_questions: On a sample of sales, how many lines were already on the check before the attendant keyed, and how many were preset keys?

already_counted.description: Check which lines the server already entered before keying the rest.

incremental.description: After a menu change, check that each preset key still sells the right item.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A cafeteria tray with no prior check: only preset keys for coffee, water and condiments are shorter, and taking payment stays as it is.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: See which clean linens, silverware, glassware, dishes or trays the station is short of.
Decide how many supplies of these items are adequate to fetch during service.
Maintain the station by carrying those clean linens, silverware, glassware, dishes and trays.

tasks.design: The attendant still looks at the station, still decides what is short, and still carries clean linens, silverware, glassware, dishes and trays from the dishwasher or the laundry store. No par level is sent to a machine, and nothing is reordered from this task. Clean stock is produced by the dishwasher and the laundry; this task only moves it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Only the person standing at the station can see that a pile is short, and only that person can carry the replacement during service.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the look or the carry. The clean items still have to be in the store, put there by the dishwasher or the laundry.
tasks.still_hard: The attendant still leaves the floor, still chooses how many to take, and still carries them back while service continues.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant can see a pile that looks full but is short of the size the next table needs, and can leave a rush table rather than walk.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the week. The attendant still keeps the station supplied by looking and carrying.

reach.task: Return clean dishes, glassware and silverware to the store
reach.learn: That this task fetches from that store and does not count the dishwasher's own stock.

reach.task: Return clean linens to the store
reach.learn: That a short station is not a linen order from this attendant.

evidence.claim: Keeping a sideboard supplied is looking and carrying. Model knowledge. A booking record does not move plates, linen or glassware.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: from seeing the station short to the clean items sitting on it. Washing, laundering and purchasing are other roles.
No structured par, sold-out flag or reorder is consumed. There is no machine step and no step at zero remaining time. The attendant decides from what they see.
Clean dishes, glassware and silverware are produced by the dishwasher. Clean linens are produced by the laundry. This task does not record a count for them.
No tool is added, so incremental upkeep is 0.
unknowns: How far the clean-stock store is from the station, which sets the carry time.
Whether the house already posts a written par. This design does not add one and does not read one.
research_questions: In one service, how many trips does the attendant make for linens, silverware, glassware, dishes or trays, and is any of that trip a written count?

incremental.description: No system is added, so there is no ongoing upkeep for this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The attendant still looks, still decides and still carries every linen, piece of silverware, glass, dish and tray. Nothing in this task is typed or reordered.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find what the customer asked for

steps.what: Locate the requested items and bring them.
Hand the located items to the customers and say what was found.

tasks.design: The attendant still hears the request and still hands the item to the customer. The locate step is the only one that shortens, and only for a regular item: a shelf label names the place, so the attendant walks there instead of opening other cupboards. The walk stays. A coat, a toy or a dish from another section has no label and is still a search of the room, inside that same step. No model picks the item.
tasks.previous_blocker: Regular items sat in unlabeled cupboards, so each request started as a search of several places.
tasks.enabler_now: A shelf label can name the place of items the station always keeps. The supervisor writes it when the station is set. No system is required.
tasks.still_hard: The attendant still hears the request, still walks, and still tells the customer. Anything off the label is still a search.
tasks.human_edge: The attendant can tell a request the house does not keep from one that is simply on the wrong shelf, and can say so without a second lap of the building.
tasks.altitude: The attendant still fetches what the guest asked for. A label removes some wrong cupboards, not the walk or the answer.

reach.task: Write the shelf label when the station is set
reach.learn: Which label to trust, and to search once when the labeled place is empty.

reach.task: Ask for the item at the table
reach.learn: To repeat the request back before leaving, so the walk is for the right item.

evidence.claim: A shelf label can name where a regular item is kept. Model knowledge. The attendant still walks and still hands the item over.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: from hearing the request to handing the item over or saying the house does not have it. Cooking the item and buying it are other roles.

Shelf-label contract: item name and place. Producer: the restaurant supervisor when the station is set. Writing the label is that supervisor's time, not this task. The attendant's reading of the label sits inside the locate step. If there is no label, the attendant searches the room inside that step. No machine step and no step at zero remaining time reads the label.
Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 is rewriting a label when a shelf moves. Hearing the request and handing the item over are not shortened.
unknowns: Which requested items are regular stock with a fixed place, and which are one-off, such as a coat or a dish from another section.
research_questions: Of the items customers ask this attendant to find in one service, how many already have a shelf label, and how many are a search of the room?

already_counted.description: Read the shelf label before walking to that place.

incremental.description: Rewrite a shelf label when a regular item moves to another place.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A request with no shelf label, such as a coat or a dish from another section: the search stays a walk, and telling the customer stays as it is.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The attendant still takes the payment, still carries the clean stock, and still walks to the item a customer asked for. An open check and a few preset keys shorten only the keying. A shelf label shortens only a search of the wrong cupboard. Nothing is reordered by a machine, and nothing is fetched by one.
reach: Server: a check with items missing. Learn which lines are already entered before adding one.
Restaurant supervisor: a preset key or a shelf label that is wrong. Learn to refuse a key that does not match the menu, and to search once when a label points at an empty place.
Dishwasher and laundry: clean stock not back in the store. Learn to fetch only what the station is short of, and not to count their stock.
Customer: an item the house does not keep. Learn to say so at the table rather than search the whole building.
skills_to_grow: Reject a check that does not match the tray before taking payment.
Reject a trip to the store when the station is not actually short.
Reject a shelf label that points at an empty place, and search once rather than trust it.
role.ambitious_version: Open checks, preset keys and shelf labels are already in place. The attendant's time stays on the guest, the tray and the walk. Payment, the carry and the hand-over do not move to a machine.

job.title: Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants and Bartender Helpers
